etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English summary, from Medieval Latin summārius, from Latin summa (“total, sum”) + -ārius (suffix forming adjectives).

definitions.definition: Concise, brief or presented in a condensed form
Performed speedily and without formal ceremony.
(law) Performed by omitting the procedures of a full trial.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Medieval Latin summārium, from Latin summa (“total, sum”) + -ārium (suffix forming nouns of purpose).

definitions.definition: An abstract or a condensed presentation of the substance of a body of material.
